Enzyme formation is controlled by separate regulatory genes, allowing precise regulation of enzyme activity. 1.1.9 WATER Water is the most common inorganic substance in cells, forming a significant part of all living organisms, whether on land or in water. It constitutes 60%-70% of body weight and occupies 75%-90% of the protoplasm. While it doesn't provide energy, water is crucial for sustaining life.

Figure 1.1.25 Water Molecules Structurally, the water molecule, H2O, is composed of two hydrogen atoms and one oxygen. It behaves as a dipole, with the oxygen atom sharing electrons with two hydrogen atoms. This creates a slightly positive end and a slightly negative end, leading to weak hydrogen bonding and the formation of a lattice structure.

Biological Functions of Water 1. Water acts as an effective solvent, dissolving soluble materials. 2. It participates in ionic reactions, aiding ionization in water. 3. It facilitates heat loss with minimal water loss, contributing to cooling through evaporation of sweat. 4. High surface tension and cohesion enable water conduction through plant xylem vessels. 5. It serves as a medium for transporting substances like nutrients in the body. 6. It provides an environment for organisms living in water. 7. It eliminates waste products in solution form, primarily as urine and to a lesser extent as sweat, maintaining homeostasis.
